messages:
Mia: Quick check — customer wants wording for SOC2 section about how we redact PII from auth/audit logs. They asked specifically about user IDs and session tokens. Need a 2-3 sentence answer I can paste.
Devon: Short version: redact at ingest, never store raw tokens, store deterministic hash for correlation only. Example we use HMAC-SHA256 with an app-only key: `logs.user_id = hmac_sha256(user_id, APP_LOG_KEY)` — no raw user IDs are kept.
Samir: Add that session tokens are never logged. We persist token_type + token_hash only. For encryption: logs at rest use envelope encryption with KMS; transit is TLS 1.2+. Key rotation policy in the repo.
Mia: @Priya can we include Datadog in the subprocessors list for observability? Customer asked whether third parties can see cleared logs.
Priya: Datadog is in-scope for production observability only. We have a signed DPA and use scoped API keys & IP allowlists. Approve including Datadog in the answer. :white_check_mark:
accessctl-bot: Access request #3421: `datadog-observe` read -> approved by Priya at 1965432205
Devon: Suggested 2-line customer blurb: "Logs are redacted at ingest to remove PII and sensitive tokens. We never store raw session tokens; persisted fields are protected with envelope encryption (KMS) and subject to quarterly key rotation and audit logging." Feel free to shorten.
Samir: For the dataflow diagram mention: app -> log-collector (redact) -> kafka -> redact-consumer -> secure-s3 (encrypted). Also note access to logs requires approval and is recorded in audit logs.
Mia: I'll paste that. Also adding one sentence about access controls: "Production log access requires approvals and is limited by role-based policies; all access is logged." Anyone object?
Priya: No objections. Also remind legal to attach subprocessors list and latest DPA copy when sending.
Mia: Thanks — sending now. :pray:
